source_title: European Parliament New European Agenda for Culture implementation report
unit_or_scope: cultural relations and diplomacy across EU and partner contexts
direct_observation: Cultural relations are described as reciprocal non-coercive interaction while cultural diplomacy is more state-led and can be instrumentalised
missing_stage: reciprocal power local benefit remedy and later geopolitical behavior
evidence_status: high for distinction; medium for outcomes
next_test: code one exchange for agenda power and participant response

source_title: UNESCO Participatory and integrated approaches in cultural governance
direct_observation: Cultural governance frequently connects foreign affairs economy/business and education; participatory governance and civil society are emphasized
missing_stage: local cultural rights benefit and policy durability
evidence_status: high for architecture; medium for effects
next_test: match one programme budget across ministries and civil-society decisions

source_title: UN Peacebuilding community-engagement guidelines and Niger example
unit_or_scope: conflict-affected communities including Diffa and Tillabéri
direct_observation: Community-specific analysis local civil-society mapping and locally identified cultural festivals support reintegration and social cohesion work
missing_stage: continued local control changed relationships safety and recurrence
evidence_status: high for process; medium for outcomes
next_test: follow peace committee and participant outcomes after event

source_title: Council of Europe Intercultural Cities interaction checklist
unit_or_scope: intercultural city policy and everyday encounters
direct_observation: Meaningful interaction is more likely under equal status common objectives and cooperation; housing education sport commerce and culture shape contact
missing_stage: prejudice change resource equality conflict remedy and belonging
evidence_status: high for framework; medium for measured effects
next_test: compare participant status and repeated cross-group contact

source_title: UNESCO Culture for Peace independent expert group report
direct_observation: Local governments communities and civil society are identified as frontline actors; locally led cultural peacebuilding memory work and ethical digital infrastructure are recommended
missing_stage: named programme peace safety cultural-rights remedy and policy change
evidence_status: medium for principles; low for causal closure
next_test: build a named programme ledger with local decision and post-program behavior

source_title: British Council Connections Through Culture evaluation
unit_or_scope: 137 UK projects with six Southeast Asian countries evaluated after four years
direct_observation: 88 percent of respondents reported a continuing counterpart relationship after the project; 82 percent rated relationship equity high or very high; 78 percent reported increased capacity and confidence to address gender disability or other inequalities
closed_stage: continued relationship perceived equity and participant capability
missing_stage: independent community benefit budgetary power cultural-rights remedy and later geopolitical behavior
evidence_status: official programme evaluation; questionnaire and programme-level evidence with participant-reporting and selection limits
next_test: trace selected partners and local audiences through funding ownership repeat collaboration and later institutional or policy behavior

source_title: UNESCO Social Dialogue for Peace and Crisis Prevention in Sri Lanka
unit_or_scope: nearly 70 community-forum members in agriculture fisheries and plantation communities
direct_observation: Phase II strengthened community-forum members in policy literacy intercultural dialogue and constructive engagement with local institutions using Sinhala and Tamil dialogue spaces
closed_stage: capacity-building and access route into institutional engagement
missing_stage: official response decision change women and vulnerable-group agenda power trust safety conflict recurrence and remedy
evidence_status: official UNESCO project account; capacity outcome reported without public comparison or decision-level follow-up
next_test: follow forum recommendations to official response implementation and participant trust across Sinhala Tamil and livelihood geographies

source_title: EU-supported Strengthening Social Cohesion Project in Indonesia
unit_or_scope: 30-month project in Lampung and South Lampung with 3870 direct participants and 23 youth-led CSOs; claimed reach over 350000
direct_observation: Project used peace education youth voices intergenerational dialogue and the Lampung cultural mechanism Piil Pesenggiri; official account reports direct engagement with 3870 people and 23 CSOs and impact on more than 350000 people
closed_stage: local cultural adaptation youth-led civil-society operation and reported reach
missing_stage: participant-level cohesion trust conflict incidence institutional response durable financing and remedy
evidence_status: official EU delegation completion account; reach and narrative outcomes not causal or longitudinal evidence
next_test: compare direct participants and wider claimed reach through repeated trust cohesion safety and institutional-response measures
